item.title: Elixir v1.20: Now a gradually typed language
item.description:
📝 20, we have completed our first development milestone which is to perform type inference and gradually type check every Elixir program, without introducing type annotations. The dynamic() type Many gradual type systems have the any() type, which, from the point of view of the type system, often means “anything goes” and no type violations are reported. Therefore, Elixir’s gradual type system tags the value_or_error variable above with the type dynamic(integer() or binary()), which means the type is either integer() or binary() at runtime.
🔗 Read more: https://elixir-lang.org/blog/2026/06/03/elixir-v1-20-0-released/

item.title: Embryos shape their limbs: a key discovery of "genetic brakes"
item.description:
📝 In findings published in the journal PNAS, Kmita and her team highlight the crucial role of certain molecular systems that act as true “genetic brakes,” ensuring that development proceeds correctly. The new research at the IRCM shows that two groups of proteins, known as Polycomb complexes (PRC1 and PRC2), cooperate to silence these genes at the right time. This regulatory system helps prevent errors that could lead to congenital abnormalities.
🔗 Read more: https://nouvelles.umontreal.ca/en/article/2026/06/02/how-embryos-shape-their-limbs-a-key-discovery-of-genetic-brakes
